rationale: Sol establishes a successful code-and-verifier exchange before showing two overlapping sign-ins, the crossed pair, and recovery with a fresh attempt. That makes it the clearest entry into this chapter’s agent-host integration problem. Astra offers larger, less crowded labels for revisiting the concurrency failure, while the baseline adds the complementary reason PKCE exists: an intercepted code is insufficient without its verifier.
findings: Sol 00:01–00:09 teaches the normal exchange before B/C overlap at 00:10–00:16; Astra introduces two attempts before its first success at 00:24–00:27. Sol gives a newcomer a working model to compare with the failure.

Astra 00:12.3–00:14.5 now retains verifier B in login A before sending the crossed pair. Sol 00:16–00:21 shows the comparable B/C substitution and returned invalid_grant, making the client mistake and server response especially explicit.

Baseline 00:09–00:15 demonstrates code interception while the verifier remains private; it complements the alternatives’ concurrency lesson. The rejection now says NO TOKEN because an absent verifier should not be conflated with the alternatives’ supplied-but-mismatched verifier.

At 350px, Astra’s two transaction rows at 00:07.5 and 00:14.5 are easiest to read. Sol’s four records at 00:15.5–00:20 are denser but retain the code/challenge associations; baseline’s formula at 00:02–00:03.5 is the smallest and needs the written guide.

Sol 00:22–00:30 and Astra 00:18–00:28 recover with fresh attempts. Baseline 00:16–00:22 instead illustrates correct possession using the same code; its documented limit warns that rejected codes may need replacement. All three omit the rest of OAuth validation and cannot establish tool permissions.

Baseline resolves by 00:20 and fades at 00:22.3–00:23.4; Astra resolves around 00:26 and Sol around 00:28. Their holds make the result readable, although Sol repeats the success mechanism and baseline leaves a longer black tail. All final first/last frames match.
contentVerdict: Keep as reference. Engineers owning an OAuth connector can use the transaction-binding review and crossed-pair exercise immediately; engineers using an already configured assistant do not need PKCE as an adoption prerequisite. The guide correctly separates code protection from tool authorization, recommends a maintained library, and now explicitly binds the transaction to its initiating client and browser session. Primary-source review supports these boundaries; the exercise is proposed, not claimed to have run against a provider.
defectsFixed: Baseline: replaced invalid_grant for an absent verifier with NO TOKEN; moved the intercepted-code chip below actor labels at 00:09–00:09.8; corrected the local engine’s full-frame endpoint fade. Rerendered with bounded FFmpeg threads and attenuated audio.
Astra: made the wrongly selected verifier persist visibly in login A at 00:12.3, and updated its sequence description.
Sol: changed Agent tool to Agent host in the encoded client label and sequence description, preserving gpt-6.1-sol provenance.
Guide: added explicit initiating-client/browser-session binding and retrieval dates for the verified primary sources.
All three revised cuts have regenerated posters, final hash-bound checks, preserved authorship, and comparative editor/correction metadata.
limitations: Audio was decoded and analysed for peak levels and activity at cue windows, with spectrogram inspection; it was not physically heard. Perceptual sound quality is untested.
Visual assessment used full-duration decoded contact sheets, native and 350px beat frames, and exact boundaries; no continuous real-time playback review is claimed.
All three are narrow PKCE illustrations. Consent, redirects, TLS, issuer/client validation, resource binding, token storage and service-side permissions require the guide and implementation review.
The MCP source check covers the cited 2025-11-25 specification, not a claim that it is the newest version. No live OAuth provider integration test was performed.
The task disclosed Sol’s provenance before the blind pass; author scenes, transcripts, metadata and prior scores were withheld until the timestamped before.md was saved. Fable attempts were excluded.
Topic-only encoded and page checks were performed; whole-library release checks and publication are outside this review.
